thread:
aisha_cs: Starting Veridian "shakedown" for Dedicated quota onboarding. Objective: confirm quota commitments, autoscale hysteresis, cache priming behavior, and our customer-facing SLA messaging. Go-live target: 2026-05-12. Ops + SRE please eyeball.

---
Scope: capacity reservation, canary routing, steady-state soak, failure-injection (network drop), eval capture + retention policy, renewal-risk thresholds.
---

marc_prod: Quick note on SLA language: we promised 99.9% availability for reserved pool and <150ms p95 for critical path. Bakeoff must surface whether we need a scoped SLA exception for cold-cache starts.

lina_se: Model plan: primary rw-v2-13b-q4 (latency budget 150ms), fallback rw-v2-6b-q4. Average seq 400, bursts to 1200 token requests. We'll send synthetic prompts mirroring typical customer flows.

 tom_infra: I'll allocate a 6-GPU reserved pool (vCPU-backed routing) and set autoscale min=4, max=10 (burst to overflow). Autoscaler config: scale_up_threshold=70% GPU util, scale_down_delay=180s. Will attach a warm-cache TTL of 4h for KV entries.

 jules_sre: Proposed test window Mon 22:00-00:30 UTC. Canary 2% for first 15m, ramp to 100% over 25m, hold 40m, induce 1% packet loss for 5m to validate fallback. Any objections?

 aisha_cs: Fine. Add customer communication steps: pre-run email, 15m pre-run Slack ping, post-run short report with metrics and decision. Renewal stakeholders must be CC'd if we see >3% throttle or repeated fallbacks.

 veridian_ops: KMS requirement: Veridian rotates envelope keys every 36h. Ask: backup keys during rotation window? Also need confirmation on how long eval samples are stored.

 lina_se: We'll redact PII and retain eval outputs for 90 days by default, can shorten to 14 days if requested by ops. We'll store in s3://veridian-evals/shakedown-17299 with encryption.

 tom_infra: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/veridian-shakedown. Contingency: overflow policy -> route to hosted-fallback with token-bucket throttling (500 RPS) and incremental backoff. If fallback used >10% of total time, mark as degraded and trigger renewal review.

 marc_prod: For renewal narrative: if bakeoff fails on latency but not on correctness, we can offer a temp credit + targeted optimizations. If correctness regressions appear in >0.5% samples, escalate to model team and pause rollout.

 jules_sre: Load script example (replace prompts with customer corpus):
```
# simple k6-esque pseudo script
k6 run --vus 500 --duration 45m -e API_KEY=$REDWOOD_KEY ./scripts/veridian_shake.js
```
Collect per-token latencies, GPU util, KV cache hit ratio.

 run-bot: Pre-run checks passed: routing rules, KMS access, RBAC for s3 bucket. Smoke run: p95 132ms, errors 0.4% (retries). Dashboard: https://dash.internal/veridian/17299

 veridian_ops: One more ask: include a short walkthrough for our customer success lead on how to interpret the metrics dashboard. We'll join the post-run review.

 aisha_cs: I'll run a 30-min enablement 2026-05-08 09:00 PDT focused on dashboards, fallback timeline, and renewal playbook. @veridian_ops is that OK?

 veridian_ops: Works for us. Please add a snippet in the enablement on how to request an SLA exception and the approval flow.

 lina_se: After the soak we'll export a sample set (max 5000 examples) to the eval bucket for QA and send a short diff report comparing outputs to baseline. PII redaction policy applied.

 jules_sre: Post-run thresholds for flagging renewal risk:
- sustained errors >5% across 10m window -> immediate flag
- fallback active >10% of test duration -> flag for follow-up
- p95 latency drift >25% relative to baseline -> investigate and hold go-live

 aisha_cs: Agreed. If any flag hits, we'll run an emergency QBR within 2 business days. Otherwise we'll proceed with staged cutover per rollout playbook. Feedback form: https://short.link/veridian-feedback.

 run-bot: Load test scheduled Mon 22:00 UTC. Reminder posting 30m before run.
